title: Animals (2026 film)

text.lead: Animals is a 2026 American crime thriller film directed by Ben Affleck and written by Affleck, Connor O. McIntyre and Billy Ray. It stars Affleck, Kerry Washington, Gillian Anderson, Adriana Paz with Luis Gerardo Méndez, and Steven Yeun. The film received negative reviews from critics.
text.plot:
In the final days of the Los Angeles mayoral race, independent candidate Mark Kimball appears to be headed for a narrow defeat. He commits his remaining life savings to fund an aggressive outreach to the Latin-American vote in the community, convinced by his campaign manager Sam that they would easily be able to make the money back once he won the election. At Sam's urging, Mark does not inform his wife Abigail before signing away the money. Abigail, meanwhile, has grown increasingly distant from her husband amid his campaign, starting an affair with Ron and intending to file for divorce after the election.
On Halloween, the Kimball's son Denny goes out trick-or-treating with their housekeeper Cecilia, along with her undocumented boyfriend Ramon and his son Hector. Ramon soon leaves to pick up work in the neighborhood, leaving Cecilia in charge of the two boys. Cecilia loses sight of them as the sun sets and an unknown figure watches her.
Back at the Kimball mansion, Abigail hints of her unhappiness in her marriage while Mark tries to get her more involved in the final days of the race. Mark receives a call from an unknown number threatening to kill Denny. Initially skeptical of the call, Abigail panics when she cannot reach Cecilia on her phone. The kidnapper sends a photograph of Denny in his Halloween costume as proof, demanding that Mark deliver $7 million in cash by midnight. He alerts the Kimball's that he is watching their mansion, warning them that calling the police would get Denny killed. Mark informs Abigail that he had already committed their life savings to his campaign, but even if he had not signed it away, he still would not have been able to secure that much cash by midnight.
Sam offers up an operative known as "Dayle" that would be able to deliver the money and help deal with the kidnappers, but she would charge a 20% fee on the cash delivery regardless of the outcome of the ransom. With no other choice, the Kimball's agree to put up their mansion as collateral after she arrives. Shortly after they agree to her terms, however, Denny returns home, unaware of the kidnappers' plot. When the kidnapper calls a moment later, Mark immediately tells him off, then tries to bargain his way out of Dayle's $1.4 million fee.
Cecilia and Ramon arrive at the mansion a few moments later, with Cecilia reporting having been attacked. Mark realizes that the kidnappers had mistakenly abducted Hector when they send him another photograph, along with a recording of his refusal to pay the ransom for Hector. Sam warns that the recording being made public would destroy his standing in the Latino community and his chances of winning the election. After Dayle had previously suggested that she could have the kidnapper killed, the Kimball's agree to go ahead with the ransom, negotiating to delay the payment until the sun rises for his own safety. Mark and Sam then depart with Dayle to attend a campaign event to keep up appearances.
Taking matters into his own hands, Ramon sneaks out behind the mansion and makes his way up to the kidnapper's lookout position over the mansion. He ultimately fails to subdue the lookout, who escapes and angrily calls Mark to threaten Hector again for a ransom of $10 million. Dayle directs Mark's answers to keep the terms of the ransom as they had agreed earlier as they return to the mansion. Mark then discovers Abigail's affair with Ron on her phone, confronting her about it in their room. He breaks down and apologizes for having made her feel less than his political ambitions, then answers a call from the kidnapper to confirm the $7 million ransom with instructions to follow in the morning.
Waiting for the kidnapper to call back at 5:00 A.M., Abigail presses Mark to be honest with her about what he wanted. Candid, Mark states that he wanted to take Dayle up on her offer of having the kidnappers killed, but would not do it without Abigail's blessing for fear of her using it against him later. Abigail confesses that she wanted to fix their marriage and the two rekindle their relationship. When the kidnapper calls in the morning, the kidnapper sets the location in Frogtown. Mark says that he would go to meet the kidnapper alone, but asks Dayle to follow behind. Before he leaves, Abigail gives Mark her blessing.
On the way to the meeting, Mark discusses Dayle's terms of having the kidnapper killed. Believing that the plot was carried out by two men, Dayle charges him an additional 20% fee, playing him back a recording implicating him in conspiracy to commit murder if he does not pay. Mark agrees to her terms, then follows the kidnappers' instructions to deliver the money into a gutter out in the open. Two men then arrive to hand over Hector and take the money. Dayle's associate shoots the two men dead from a distance, but a third kidnapper kills him from a sniping position, then shoots Dayle after she arrives to recover the money. As the sniper then descends to kill Mark, he is suddenly shot in the head by Ramon. Mark recovers Dayle's phone from her before she dies, securing the evidence against his conspiracy to murder the kidnappers. Despite the kidnapper having hinted at personal motivation against Mark for their plot, Mark does not recognize him.
In exchange for allowing him to keep most of the money, Ramon helps Mark hide the corpses of all but the sniper. The Kimball's and Ramon reframe the story to the public to paint Mark as the hero who had saved Hector. Mark's support among Latino voters surges, allowing him to easily win the mayoral race and setting him up to run for higher political office.

- Ben Affleck as Mark Kimball
- Kerry Washington as Abigail Kimball
- Gillian Anderson as Dayle Burton
- Adriana Paz as Cecilia Trujillo
- Ray Fisher as Ron Sperling
- Christopher Woodley as Denny Kimball
- Luis Gerardo Méndez as Ramon
- Steven Yeun as Sam Allison
- Matt Gerald as the kidnapper / James Bureaux
- Jacob Estrada as Hector
text.production:
Development:
The film was announced in January 2024, with Ben Affleck directing, with original screenplay were co-written by Affleck, Billy Ray and Matt Damon starring. In February, Jennifer Garner was in talks to join the film. Filming was scheduled to begin in March 2024 in Los Angeles. On casting ex-wife Garner opposite Damon, Affleck said: "I thought, 'God, Jen Garner would be amazing for this role.' It also has the added benefit of, like, both of us will see our kids more because we do a week and a week and back and forth. I thought, well, we can coordinate our schedules around it. She could bring something interesting that she hasn’t [done], that I kind of know she can do, that I don’t think she had a chance to do in one movie." Gillian Anderson and Steven Yeun were also quietly cast around this time, however Affleck ultimately decided to delay the production just before filming began after getting cold feet.
A year later, in February 2025, production reignited with Damon no longer part of the cast, due to his commitment to The Odyssey, with Affleck himself taking on the lead role, and Anderson officially joining the cast. Kerry Washington (replacing Garner), Yeun, Luis Gerardo Méndez, and Adriana Paz also joined the cast in February. On replacing Garner with Washington after stepping into the lead role himself, Affleck later elaborated: "I talked to Jen, and she was like, ‘We don’t wanna do that. You just get baggage,’... I still would wanna work with her in the future, but what you don’t wanna do is take the audience’s baggage and have it work against you, you know?" In March, Ray Fisher, Mark Kassen, and Christopher Woodley joined the cast.
Filming:
Principal photography began on March 7, 2025 in Los Angeles.
text.release: Animals was released on Netflix and in select theaters on October 9, 2026.
text.reception: On the review aggregator website Rotten Tomatoes, 38% of 47 critics' reviews are positive, with an average rating of 5.4/10. Metacritic, which uses a weighted average, assigned the film a score of 33 out of 100, based on 19 critics, indicating "generally unfavorable" reviews.
